blocks.content: The institution of Lokayukta was established at the state level to inquire into allegations of corruption and maladministration against public servants.

items: Distinction Alert: Odisha passed the Lokayukta Act first (1970), whereas Maharashtra set up the institution first (1971).
Consultation Process: Mandatory consultation with both the Chief Justice of the High Court and the Leader of the Opposition in the Assembly is a frequent MCQs topic.

Variation in Jurisdiction: In some states (e.g., Himachal Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh), the Chief Minister falls under the Lokayukta's jurisdiction, while in others (e.g., Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh), the Chief Minister is excluded.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The establishment of Lokayukta was recommended by the First Administrative Reforms Commission (1966–1970) headed by Morarji Desai.
Odisha was the first state to pass the Lokayukta Act in 1970, but Maharashtra was the first to establish the institution in 1971.
The Lokayukta and Upalokayukta are appointed by the Governor of the state after consulting the Chief Justice of the High Court and the Leader of the Opposition.
The structure, jurisdiction, tenure, and conditions of service of Lokayuktas vary across different states as they are statutory bodies created by state laws.
The Lokayukta submits an annual report on performance to the Governor, which is placed before the State Legislature.
